java_locations.role: Places UCenteredCharacter at the double-precision center of the circled spot.
Computes the UnusedSpace translation as doubles and passes the Java TextLayout outline PathIterator directly to the SVG backend.
Adds double outline coordinates to the double translation and formats the resulting path coordinates to four decimal places.
Derives the glyph center on a quarter-pixel raster grid and retains it as a double.

rust_locations.role: Uses Java-compatible quarter-pixel centers but transforms integer font outline coordinates through ab_glyph's single-precision scale factor before formatting them to four places.
Uses centered_character_path generatively for every ordinary or custom class spot glyph when no oracle geometry is present.

claimed_invariant: Centered-character SVG coordinates are the embedded TrueType outline's font-unit coordinates multiplied by the requested font size divided by units-per-em, then translated by the Java-compatible quarter-pixel center and DriverCenteredCharacterSvg's half-pixel offset. Java performs the outline transform and translation in double precision and rounds only once when SvgGraphics formats each final coordinate to four decimal places.
causal_divergence: Rust obtains the mathematically identical scale through ab_glyph::ScaleFont::scale_factor, whose horizontal and vertical components are f32. Multiplying large integer font-unit coordinates by this single-precision ratio introduces errors from 0.0001px to 0.0045px before the final four-place formatting. Characters whose coordinates land away from a rounding boundary still match, while G, U, and R expose the same precision loss at different canvas translations.
planned_model_change: Keep ab_glyph's unscaled outline and the existing Java-derived UnusedSpace centers, but compute the outline transform ratio directly as f64 font_size / f64 units_per_em. Apply that double ratio to each font-unit point and perform the existing translation and four-place formatting once. Do not add character tables, per-letter offsets, fixture conditions, or tolerance.

checked_derivations.derivation: The Rust and Java command sequence, center, and every coarse coordinate agree; only final digits differ, such as expected 32.8228 versus actual 32.8227 and expected 34.0513 versus actual 34.0512. This is the signature of an upstream precision loss before identical four-place formatting, not a glyph, center, or placement mismatch.

The R outline retains its complete topology and y coordinates but Rust x coordinates differ by 0.0044-0.0045px throughout the contour. A constant translation of the same outline through a single-precision scale explains the coherent residual; changing the character center or entity layout would move the ellipse or produce larger quarter-pixel deltas.

perturbation_axes: custom and default spot characters across the printable ASCII range
one-leaf EntityImageDegenerated and linked SVEK bodies
renamed labels and changed spot colors
scope_boundary: This mechanism owns numeric precision in the TrueType outline-to-SVG transform for centered characters. It does not own font selection, UnusedSpace center derivation, glyph topology, class header layout, spot color/style resolution, arbitrary text rendering, comparator tolerance, or corpus eligibility.
acceptance: All four evidence inputs become structurally equivalent without oracle data.
Existing default C, E, A, and I spot paths do not regress.
A fresh multi-character perturbation proves one double-precision transform handles changed characters and placements without character-specific data.
The full no-oracle ratchet does not regress any family.
Renderer tests, clippy, and the four frozen mechanical guards pass except for explicitly pre-existing gate debt.
An independent checker records a verdict at the exact implementation revision.
forbidden_approaches: per-character path literals or coordinate offsets
